segments.text: Building a society from the refuse of the divine.

When the heavens went silent, the concept of "Divine Right" evaporated. There were no longer any gods to mandate who sat on the throne, and the blood of ancient lineages proved useless against the dissolving world.
In the vacuum left by the Sundering, the survivors looked for anyone who could keep their roof from collapsing.

The entities that rose to fill this void are not defined by borders, patriotism, or culture, but by the necessities they monopolize. The Greywater Compact turned peace into a subscription service, enforcing law only where the ledger balances.
To move gold and words across the broken lands requires paying the toll of the Halcyon League.

Even the end of the world has been commercialized; the Weave sells protection from the Rifts to the highest bidder, while the Speculars market the ultimate luxury to those who can no longer stand the noise: a new way of life, or a sweet, blissful silence.

For the common citizen, this shift has fundamentally altered the social contract. One no longer pledges allegiance to a faction, but signs a contract with them. The relationship is pragmatic and transactional. You are safe only as long as you are solvent.

This has created a geopolitical landscape that is fluid and ruthless. A city might be geographically located in the Remosan Empire, legally contracted to the Greywater Compact for police services, and reliant on the Halcyon League for its banking.
Sovereignty in Virelia is a tangled web of receipts and debts. A city might sit geographically in the Remosan empire, contract the Greywater compact for police, and bank through the Halcyons.
